leverage.exposure: A leveraged position is open and has been for days. It is not yet urgent — the lock is still more than two days away — but it has only one way out and no reason to wait. Execute the sale and the exposure closes; leave it and every hour that passes is an hour closer to a matchday that scores nothing at all.

binding_gap: There is no positional gap. The binding constraint is the negative balance, and it has exactly one legal remedy: a single sale large enough to clear it. That is what ranks the Treu sale above everything else on the board.

verdict.headline: Unchanged and still binding: sell Philipp Treu back to Kickbase now.

verdict.detail: Unchanged and still binding: sell Philipp Treu back to Kickbase now. The balance is negative, a negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the whole of MD5, and Treu is the only body that clears the deficit on its own at the lowest cost in points. Nothing else on the board earns an action this run — no points buy clears, and no listing qualifies for the tick flip. Quiet run; the page carries it.

sell.reason: Philipp Treu, defender, SC Freiburg. Instant-sell to Kickbase, which pays exactly market value with no spread. He is fit, he is in Freiburg's probable eleven, and he is not being sold because anything is wrong with him — he is sold because he is the smallest body that individually covers the deficit. Of the five bodies large enough, Neuer, Engelhardt, Nusa and Guirassy all carry far higher season averages, so each of them costs more points to give up. One decision was re-examined and rejected this run: holding Treu until just before the lock would capture two market-value ticks and a little more cash, but the gain is a fraction of a percent of team value against the risk of carrying a negative balance for another two days, and a run of bad ticks could leave him too small to clear the deficit at all. Clear it at the first opportunity, not the last.

movers.reason: No qualifying flip. Of everything on the board, exactly one Kickbase listing is a rising player priced at market value with no manager ask attached — Sebastiaan Bornauw — and he fails on timing alone: his auction ends after the last market-value update that falls before the lock, so winning him captures no tick and he would have to be unwound for nothing. Everything else on the board is flat or falling, and buying a faller at market value is the measured inverse of the edge. The drift itself is unchanged for an eighth consecutive run, with no sign of rivals crowding in. One new observation worth watching rather than acting on: the largest board listing this ledger has ever recorded cleared slightly below market value, uncontested, on the same night three cheap listings cleared between sixteen and fifty-one per cent above it. If contest really does thin out as the ticket grows, flip capital belongs in one large rising listing rather than spread across several cheap ones — but that needs the premium band split by listing size, which needs the ledger database, which is still unreachable. Two questions remain open and unresolved: whether Kickbase caps squad size, which would cap flip throughput; and the fact that the drift edge is measured in one league over one period and will decay if rivals crowd in.
